Hi all —

I've sketched a detailed benchmarking matrix and some proposed SLOs. Key items below; I'll attach the CSV matrix to the MAP draft. Please call out any workload we should add.

Workload definitions (canonical runs):
- Chat (low-latency, multi-turn): 1k requests, sequence lengths: median 48 tokens, 90th 220 tokens, model variants: small/medium/large (fp16 + 4-bit quant), context window up to 2,048 tokens. Key test modes: cold cache (first token), warm prefix cache (simulated ongoing session).
- Completions / batch scoring (throughput-focused): 10k requests batched into micro-batches (batch sizes 8/32/128), average prompt 120 tokens. Measure tokens/sec and GPU utilization.
- Embeddings (if Octane uses for semantic match): 5k vectors, vector dim depends on model; measure QPS and microsecond latency distribution.

Metrics (definitions):
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): measured from request arrival to emission of first token (ms). Report P50/P90/P95/P99.
- Token latency (per-token): average and tail for token generation (ms/token).
- End-to-end request latency (ms) for chat turn.
- Throughput: tokens/sec sustained over a 5-minute window and peak tokens/sec. Also requests/sec for concurrency windows.
- Resource metrics: GPU memory, GPU utilization, kernel stall time (where observable).

Proposed success criteria (example baseline for pilot):
- TTFT P95 <= 450ms for chat (warm cache), P99 <= 800ms
- End-to-end P95 for chat turns <= 650ms
- Sustained throughput for batch scoring >= 15k tokens/sec on a 4-GPU pool (our dedicated SKU)
- No request error rate > 0.1% during 30-minute sustained runs

Concurrency matrix: single-user baseline, 10 concurrent sessions, 50 concurrent sessions (peak), 200 concurrent sessions (stress). We'll flag the run where latency degrades beyond SLOs.

Test harness and methodology highlights:
- Use the same client-side request pacing as production (exponential inter-arrival where appropriate)
- Run each cell 3x and report median of medians; keep both raw and aggregated artifacts
- Separate cold-start runs (clean runtime) from warm runs (populated KV cache)
- Track model variant differences and quantization trade-offs; we can recommend a quantized profile if quality holds

Deliverables and timeline (recommended):
- Day 0-2: Finalize workload matrix (this week)
- Day 3-9: Execute runs (canonical matrix across 3 model variants)
- Day 10-12: Analyze and produce results page + MAP update

I attached the benchmark_matrix_v1.csv (columns: workload_id, model_variant, batch_size, concurrency, seq_stats, runs).

-- Marcus Lin
Sr. Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marcus — this looks thorough and exactly what we need. Couple clarifications before you run: 

- For chat median/90th token counts: our telemetry shows median ~60 tokens, 90th ~180 tokens. Use those numbers instead of the ones you listed.
- Peak concurrency: we can expect ~120 concurrent active sessions during a marketing spike (about 3x baseline). Use 120 as the peak concurrency target.
- Cold vs warm: good to have both; note Octane will likely route returning users to a sticky session so warm cache behavior matters more.

If the proposed success criteria (TTFT P95 <= 450ms, throughput >=15k tokens/sec) are achievable, Octane can commit to the production pilot sign-off. We also need the MAP to include a go/no-go decision point: if P95 TTFT > 650ms in warm runs for our median workload, Octane will request either tuning (batching/quantization) or an extended pilot with reduced SLA.

Can you run the canonical matrix with the revised token distribution (median 60 / 90th 180) and send preliminary results by end of week?

Best —
Ivy
